problems.title: A sine with a quadratic input
problems.question: Find the minimum of sin(x²-πx/3) over real x.
problems.idea: The sine never falls below -1; check that its input can reach an angle attaining that bound.
steps: The quadratic input equals (x-π/6)²-π²/36, so its range extends without bound upward.
In particular, it can equal 3π/2: the equation (x-π/6)²=3π/2+π²/36 has real solutions.
At either such input, the sine is -1, attaining its absolute lower bound.

problems.title: Parallel lines inside a plane
problems.question: No point of line a lies in plane w. How many lines in w are parallel to a?
problems.idea: A line disjoint from a plane has a direction parallel to that plane.
formulas: Through every point in a plane there is one line with any specified in-plane direction.
steps: Line a is parallel to w because it never intersects it.
Its direction therefore occurs among the lines in w.
Infinitely many different parallel translates of that direction lie in w.

problems.title: Use quadrant signs in an addition formula
problems.question: cosα=3/5 with α in quadrant I; sinβ=3/5 with β in quadrant II. Find sin(α+β).
problems.idea: Recover the missing sine and cosine with their correct signs.
steps: Since α is in quadrant I, sinα=4/5. Since β is in quadrant II, cosβ=-4/5.

problems.title: Reduce shifted sine signs
problems.question: In which quadrant is α if sin(α-11π/2)>0 and sin(α-π)>0?
problems.idea: Use periodicity to replace each shifted sine by a basic sine or cosine.
steps: The first condition gives cosα>0.
The second gives sinα<0.
Positive cosine and negative sine identify quadrant IV.

problems.title: Combine two standard-angle values
problems.question: Evaluate $\sin(4\pi/3)+\tan150^\circ$.
problems.idea: Convert each to its exact signed value.
steps: Using denominator 2√3 gives -3/(2√3)-2/(2√3).
The sum is -5/(2√3).

problems.title: Equal inclined segments with perpendicular projections
problems.question: Two equal segments from a point outside a plane make a 60° angle. Their projections in the plane are perpendicular. Find each segment’s inclination to the plane.
problems.idea: Their common vertical component is the only contribution to the dot product.
steps: Let each segment length be L and the perpendicular height be h.
The horizontal projection dot product is zero, so the full dot product is h².
Thus h²=L²cos60°=L²/2, giving h/L=1/√2.
The inclination is arcsin(1/√2)=45°.

problems.title: Shift identities make the expression constant
problems.question: Evaluate $\frac{\sin(\pi+\alpha)}{\sin(3\pi/2-\alpha)}-\frac{\tan(3\pi/2+\alpha)}{\cot(\pi-\alpha)}+\tan(\pi-\alpha)+1$ at α=199.
problems.idea: Simplify symbolically before using the numerical input.
steps: The first fraction is tanα. The second fraction is 1 wherever the original expression is defined.
Also tan(π-α)=-tanα.
The whole expression is tanα-1-tanα+1=0.
At the stated input α=199 radians the original denominators are nonzero.

problems.title: A double-angle sine from a tangent
problems.question: If tanα=a, find sin2α.
problems.idea: Divide the double-angle identity by sin²α+cos²α.
steps: Because tanα exists, cosα≠0.
Thus sin2α=2tanα/(1+tan²α).
Substitute a to obtain 2a/(1+a²).

problems.title: Read the superscript degree marks correctly
problems.question: Order a=sin140°, b=cos40°, c=tan47° increasingly.
problems.idea: Use complementary angles and compare with 45°.
steps: We have b<1, while tan47°>tan45°=1, so b<c.
Therefore a<b<c.
problems.note: The original Word runs confirm 140°,40°,47°. Their superscript zeros denote degrees and are not extra digits in 1400,400,470.

problems.title: Unsigned distances allow several plane positions
problems.question: The distances from consecutive square vertices A,B,C to a plane are 6,7,8. Find the distance from D.
problems.idea: Signed distances are affine over a parallelogram, but the given ordinary distances have unknown signs.
formulas: Signed distances satisfy sA+sC=sB+sD, so sD=sA+sC-sB.
steps: If A,B,C are on the same side, the signed values 6,7,8 give sD=7, hence distance 7.
Allowing the plane to separate vertices gives other possibilities: (6,-7,8) gives 21; (6,7,-8) gives -9; (-6,7,8) gives -5.
Changing all signs does not change the resulting ordinary distance. These sign combinations exhaust the possibilities.
problems.answer: Possible distances: 5,7,9,21. The listed values 5,7,9 are all possible; 7 uses the same-side assumption.
problems.note: No condition says that the square lies entirely on one side of the plane. Without it, the question has multiple valid choices.

problems.title: Inclination from a segment’s endpoint heights
problems.question: AB=13 cm does not cross a plane. Its endpoint distances to the plane are 6 and 11 cm. Find the cotangent of the line-plane angle.
problems.idea: Both endpoints are on the same side, so the perpendicular component is their height difference.
steps: The perpendicular component is 11-6=5.
The projection is √(13²-5²)=12.
Therefore cotθ=12/5=2.4.

problems.title: Two segments between parallel planes
problems.question: Parallel planes contain A,C on one plane and B,D on the other. AB=17,CD=10, and the projection of AB has length 15. Find the tangent of CD’s inclination.
problems.idea: Both segments span the same perpendicular plane separation.
steps: From AB, the plane separation is h=√(17²-15²)=8.
For CD, its projection is √(10²-8²)=6.
Hence tanθ=8/6=4/3.

problems.title: Signs after removing whole turns
problems.question: Which are positive: I sin150°, II sin670°, III tan210°?
problems.idea: Reduce to familiar quadrants.
formulas: Sine is positive in quadrants I,II; tangent in I,III.
steps: 670° is congruent to 310°, in quadrant IV, so its sine is negative.
210° is in quadrant III, where tangent is positive.

problems.title: Range of a quadratic in sinx
problems.question: Find the range of y=sin²x+sinx.
problems.idea: Set t=sinx, with -1≤t≤1.
steps: The minimum is -1/4, attained at t=-1/2.
The endpoint values are 0 at t=-1 and 2 at t=1, so the maximum is 2.
Every intermediate t and hence every intermediate y is attained.

problems.title: Antipodal points make a right triangle
problems.question: Distinct points A=(cost,sint),B=(-cost,-sint),C=(cos(1-t),sin(1-t)) form a triangle. Classify it.
problems.idea: All three points lie on the unit circle, and AB is a diameter.
formulas: cos²u+sin²u=1; an inscribed angle subtending a diameter is 90°.
steps: A and B are opposite points of the unit circle.
C lies on the same circle and is distinct from both.
Therefore ACB is a right angle.
problems.answer: A right triangle, with the right angle at C.

problems.title: Possible values of tangent plus cotangent
problems.question: Which listed value can tanα+cotα have: -√3,-√5,√1.2,-√2,1?
problems.idea: Use t+1/t for nonzero real t.
steps: The possible values lie in (-∞,-2]∪[2,∞).
Among the choices, only -√5 has magnitude at least 2.
It is attainable: t+1/t=-√5 has roots t=(-√5±1)/2, both nonzero real numbers.

problems.title: Common intersection of three pairwise nonparallel planes
problems.question: Three distinct planes are pairwise nonparallel. What can their common intersection be?
problems.idea: Intersect two planes first, then compare their line with the third plane.
formulas: Two distinct nonparallel planes meet in a line; a line and plane meet in a line, a point, or the empty set.
steps: If the third plane contains the first two planes’ intersection line, the common set is that line.
If it crosses that line at one point, the common set is one point.
If it is parallel to that line and disjoint, the common set is empty, even while it intersects each original plane separately.
problems.answer: A line, a point, or the empty set.

problems.title: A point equally far from a right triangle’s vertices
problems.question: S is 17 cm from each vertex of a right triangle with legs 18 and 24 cm. Find its distance to the triangle’s plane.
problems.idea: The perpendicular projection is the circumcentre.
formulas: Right-triangle circumradius=half the hypotenuse; equal-distance point height satisfies h²+R²=L².
steps: The hypotenuse is √(18²+24²)=30, so R=15.
The projection of S is the circumcentre because equal distances give equal projected distances to the vertices.

problems.title: A trigonometric square reduces to one
problems.question: Simplify $[1/(1+\tan^2x)-\sin^2x+2\sin^2x\cot x]^2-\sin4x$, where sin2x≠0.
problems.idea: Rewrite the bracket in double-angle form.
steps: The bracket is cos²x-sin²x+sin2x=cos2x+sin2x.
Its square is cos²2x+sin²2x+2sin2xcos2x=1+sin4x.
Subtracting sin4x leaves 1.

problems.title: Count pairs of skew cube edges
problems.question: How many unordered pairs of cube edges lie on skew lines?
problems.idea: Count the skew partners of one edge, then divide by two.
formulas: Unordered pair count=(number of edges·partners per edge)/2.
steps: A cube has 12 edges. For one chosen edge, 4 others meet it at its endpoints and 3 others are parallel to it.
Excluding those and the edge itself leaves 12-4-3-1=4 skew partners.
Thus the number is 12·4/2=24.

problems.title: Two equal spatial segments and their projections
problems.question: A is 2 units above a plane; B,C lie in it, AB=AC=3, and the angle between their projections is 60°. Find BC.
problems.idea: The projections have equal length.
steps: Let O be the perpendicular foot of A. Then OB=OC=√(3²-2²)=√5.
In triangle BOC, the included angle is 60°.
Thus BC²=5+5-2·5·cos60°=5, giving BC=√5.

problems.title: Equal distance from a square’s four vertices
problems.question: A square has side a. A point M is distance b from each vertex. Find its perpendicular distance to the square’s plane.
problems.idea: Its projection is the square centre.
steps: The centre-to-vertex squared distance is a²/2.
The spatial equal-distance condition gives h²=b²-a²/2.
Take the nonnegative square root. A real configuration requires b≥a/√2.
problems.note: The source’s reference to a “triangle plane” is a wording slip; the four square vertices determine the plane used here.

problems.title: Reduce a large degree angle
problems.question: Evaluate $(\tan2100^\circ-\cot2100^\circ)\cos2100^\circ$.
problems.idea: Use tangent’s 180° period and cosine’s 360° period.
steps: Their difference is -2/√3; cos2100°=1/2.
The product is -1/√3.

problems.title: When a double-angle sine is positive
problems.question: In which quadrants can x lie if sin2x>0?
problems.idea: Use the signs in sin2x=2sinxcosx.
formulas: A product is positive when its nonzero factors have the same sign.
steps: Sine and cosine are both positive in quadrant I.
They are both negative in quadrant III.
In quadrants II and IV their signs differ, so the product is negative.
problems.answer: Quadrant I or III, excluding the axes.

problems.title: Sixth and fourth powers from sin2x
problems.question: If sin2x=1/4, find (sin⁶x+cos⁶x)/(sin⁴x+cos⁴x).
problems.idea: Set u=sin²x,v=cos²x and use u+v=1.
steps: The numerator is 1-3/64=61/64. The denominator is 1-2/64=62/64.
Their quotient is 61/62.
